| `disk-win.img`, `testfs1-win` | Generated by `scripts/make_win_fixture.py` from `testfs1-af`: synthetic Windows artifacts (hives including UsrClass.dat with ShellBags and SYSTEM with BAM/DAM, a SRUM database (SRUDB-4k.dat), a Wi-Fi profile XML, four scheduled tasks (task files and TaskCache: one of Windows' own, one from C:\Users\Public, one hidden Tarrask-style, one without a task file), Internet Explorer index.dat files (daily and main history, cache with a LEAK entry, a download; deleted entries inside them), deleted registry keys and values in free cells of NTUSER.DAT and UsrClass.dat, a UsrClass.dat not yet flushed with its .LOG1 (new-format log entry), event logs, Prefetch, LNK, Jump Lists, a change journal $UsnJrnl with a sparse start, a folder known only from the journal, an SDelete rename chain and a version 3 record) at their real paths, plus carving ground truth from `scripts/fixture_carve.py` (files in free clusters, a deleted picture whose clusters are free, samples, lookalikes, a deleted index.dat with two loose IE records, and a cut-off JPEG in a 2 MiB unpartitioned tail). Invented data: LAB-PC, documentation IP ranges, `.test` domains | as `testfs1` |
| `bitlocker-xts.img`, `bitlocker-xts.BEK` | Generated by `cargo test -p kokino-image make_bitlocker_fixture -- --ignored`: `testfs1-win` encrypted in a BitLocker volume (AES-128-XTS, as Windows 10 makes it) with three protectors: password `Lab-Pa55`, recovery password `111111-222222-333333-444444-555555-666666-000077-123453` and a startup key (`bitlocker-xts.BEK`, 156 bytes). The metadata and the boot sector copy sit in a 256 KiB tail after the NTFS volume. Test data, not a real key | as `testfs1` |

Invented data | as `testfs1` |

| `win/ese-deep.dat` | Generated by `scripts/make_srum_fixture.py deep` (Windows only): an ESE database written by esent.dll with one table of 400 rows and 180-byte keys, so its B+ tree has three levels (the root carries neither the leaf nor the parent-of-leaf flag), and UTF-16 text in a column declared as code page 1252. Invented data | as `testfs1` |
| `win/SRUDB.dat`, `win/SRUDB-4k.dat` | Generated by `scripts/make_srum_fixture.py` (Windows only): SRUM databases written by Windows' own esent.dll, with 32 KiB and 4 KiB pages, SRUM's table and column names, 7-bit compressed ids, a 303-row network table spread over several pages, and the ground truth listed in the script. Unused pages at the end are cut off. Invented data | as `testfs1` |
| `win/` | Generated by `scripts/fixture_windows.py`: the same artifacts as single files, plus LZXPRESS Huffman vectors produced by Windows' own `RtlCompressBuffer` | as `testfs1` |
| `hfsplus.img`, `apfs.img`, `mac-manifest.txt` | Made with hdiutil, ditto and the shell on GitHub's macOS runner by `scripts/make_mac_fixture.sh` (workflow "Mac test images"): a journaled HFS+ volume and a GPT disk with an APFS container, each with folders, a hard link, a symlink, extended attributes (one a quarantine flag), an LZVN-compressed file, a Unicode name and a deleted file. `mac-manifest.txt` is what macOS reported about every file (the tests' ground truth) | Invented data |
| `iso-rr-joliet.iso`, `iso-udf.iso`, `iso-multisession.iso` | Built with mkisofs 2.01 by `scripts/make_iso_fixture.py`: Rock Ridge + Joliet, the same with a UDF 1.02 bridge (one UDF entry then marked deleted), and two sessions where the second drops `secret-plan.txt` and adds `added-later.txt`. This mkisofs build records times one hour early (summer time mix-up); the tests check what the disc says | Invented data |
| `vd-*.vhd`, `vd-*.vhdx`, `vd-*.vmdk` | Generated by `scripts/make_vdisk_fixture.py` from `disk-fat.img`: the same disk as dynamic VHD, VHDX, VMDK (sparse, streamOptimized, flat, split), and differencing VHD, VHDX and a VMDK snapshot that add a known 1.5 KiB patch on top of their parent. 7-Zip reads the VHD and VMDK files back to the same bytes. `vd-vmware-stream.vmdk` was written by VMware ovftool 4.4 (OVF export of a VM using `vd-sparse.vmdk`) | Invented data |
| `ext2.img`, `ext3.img`, `ext4.img` | Generated by `scripts/make_ext_fixture.py` (pure Python, no mkfs needed): files in nested folders, a hard link, a fast symlink, a fragmented file (ext4) or one through an indirect block (ext2/3), a deleted file whose name survives in directory slack, and an orphaned deleted inode. ext3 and ext4 zero the deleted inodes' block maps as the kernel does; their journal holds a copy of the inode table from before the delete. 7-Zip reads all three | Invented data |
| `linux-server.img` | Generated by the same script: an ext4 Debian-like server (hostname lab-srv, zone Europe/Skopje) with accounts, auth.log and syslog in classic format, wtmp, btmp, a journal file (two messages stored XZ- and LZ4-compressed), a mail spool /var/mail/alice (two messages, MIME with a PDF attachment) and a saved .eml, shell histories, dpkg and apt logs, cron, a systemd unit, ld.so.preload, SSH keys, NetworkManager, DHCP lease and /etc/hosts entries telling one intrusion story | Invented data (TEST-NET addresses, .test domains, fake password hashes) |
| `fat12.img`, `fat16.img`, `fat32.img`, `exfat.img`, `disk-fat.img` | Generated by `scripts/make_fat_fixture.py` (pure Python, no mkfs needed): the same small story on each file system (a fragmented long-named file, a deleted file with free clusters, a deleted file whose clusters were reused, a deleted folder) and an MBR disk with the FAT32 and exFAT volumes as two partitions. The FAT32 volume has fewer clusters than Microsoft's FAT32 minimum to stay small; Kokino and Linux go by its layout, Windows would not mount it | Invented data |
| `photo/` | Generated by `scripts/make_photo_fixture.py` (Pillow, numpy): a synthetic "camera" photo with custom tables, EXIF, GPS and thumbnail, and variants with known findings (edited with the old thumbnail kept, re-saved with libjpeg tables, cropped, double-compressed, ZIP appended, cloned region, PNG and BMP with LSB-embedded data in the first 30%) | Invented data |
